text:
sarah: Customer acme-inc (acct: ACME-882) opened a support ticket: model responses intermittently produce invalid JSON when using json_mode=strict. ~18% of requests yesterday failed schema validation and triggered retries, customer reports billing spike and degraded UX. Attaching short repro below.

devin: Can you paste the exact request they sent and a raw response example? Is this only with streaming=true?

sarah: Repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","json_mode":"strict","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"order":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"integer"},"amount":{"type":"number"},"status":{"type":"string","enum":["created","paid","failed"]}},"required":["id","amount","status"]}},"required":["order"]},"prompt":"Return a JSON object with an 'order' object."}'
```

sarah: Raw response body we captured (note this one is from a streaming session):
```
{"order":{"id":10234,"amount":"79.99","status":"paid"}
```
(Notice the amount is a string not a number, and streaming ended before final newline/EOF in some cases causing missing trailing newline; in other failures the final `}` is present but types are wrong.)

jin: Two separate issues: a) type mismatch (amount as string) and b) streaming truncation/partial frames causing parse/validation failure. Did they also hit an auth rotation or rate limit around the same time?

sarah: They said auth rotation for their API key happened ~2026-03-02 14:10 UTC. We see a cluster of 401s around then, and a spike in client retries. Logs: `proxy: 401 token rotated -> client retries 3x -> 200 but streamed output sometimes truncated`.

devin: Dev note: when clients retry quickly against streaming endpoints we can end up with interleaved chunks or canceled streams. Need to check our connection cleanup hooks. Also the strict schema path rejects string-number coercion. Is customer using schema with `type:number`?

sarah: Yes, their schema expects `amount` number. They said historically model returned a number but after a recent model rollout some responses started quoting amounts (probably because prompt asked for a currency string in other contexts).

emily: Billing impact: their account had ~12k extra tokens billed because each retry is a new request. They want a credit for the retry-induced spike.

devin: Action items I'm proposing: 1) Eng-runtime: investigate streaming connection termination behavior and ensure aborted streams don't produce partial responses to the validation layer. 2) ML/onboarding: add robustness in our parsing step to detect incomplete JSON from stream and wait short grace period for remaining frames before failing. 3) Support: suggest temporary mitigations for customer.

jin: Quick mitigation for customer: set `json_mode` to `permissive` or post-process by running a small sanitization step: coerce numeric strings to numbers and allow null/empty to be treated as missing. Also they can switch streaming=false to force full-body responses while we debug.

sarah: I already suggested switching streaming=false and `json_mode:permissive`. Customer tried non-streaming for 100 reqs and saw 0 parse errors. They prefer streaming for latency though.

devin: For our internal prioritization: label as P1 for runtime streaming correctness + P2 for schema coercion guidance. Do we have a simple unit test to reproduce interleaved/truncated frames? If not I’ll add one.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: A small fix to connection cleanup is scheduled on prod-canary at 2334568100, rollback window 30m.

jin: When you add the unit test, include two things: 1) simulate client reconnects mid-stream, 2) simulate model token variations that sometimes emit quoted numbers. We should catch both.

emily: On the billing side, I can approve a one-off credit if support documents the retry windows. Please attach request IDs and token volumes.

sarah: Done — uploaded logs and request IDs to the case. Also customer asked whether our parser ever coerces types automatically in strict mode? We should clarify in docs: strict==no coercion.

devin: Agreed. We should update docs and error message to be explicit: `strict` mode will fail on type mismatches and incomplete JSON; use `permissive` to allow basic coercion or supply a preflight step.

sarah: Next steps: Devin to triage runtime fix and add test; Jin to propose short buffering/window for streaming validator; Emily to process billing credit; Support to follow up with customer and recommend non-streaming until canary fix verifies.

devin: I'll open ENG-RT-4721 and link this thread. ETA for canary verification end of day.

sarah: Customer aware and will wait on canary results. They asked if we can provide a short snippet to sanitize the model output in client code — suggested example: `if (typeof order.amount === 'string' && order.amount.match(/^\d+\.?\d*$/)) order.amount = parseFloat(order.amount)` — will send that.

jin: Also adding note: if schema includes `enum`, casing differences still cause strict failures. Recommend canonicalizing enums in prompt or using case-insensitive validator for enums where acceptable.

sarah: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and mark for escalation. :white_check_mark:
